name: The Indie Coffee Illusion
partSub: Sunlight, smooth jazz, and the myth of romantic hospitality

lines.text: Every weekend in Indiranagar, thousands of young techies walk past glass storefronts filled with warm sunlight, smooth jazz, and the intoxicating aroma of freshly roasted Ethiopian beans.
lines.title: THE SUNLIT SPECIALTY OASIS
lines.subtitle: Glass storefronts, smooth jazz, and Ethiopian roast aroma

lines.text: It feels peaceful, romantic, and effortlessly profitable. My name is Anurag Bansal, and welcome to Not a Startup.
lines.title: NOT A STARTUP EXCLUSIVE
lines.subtitle: My name is Anurag Bansal, and let's decode the real balance sheet

lines.text: On paper, specialty coffee is an arithmetic dream. Roasted green beans cost sixty rupees. Oat milk costs thirty. You sell a cup for two hundred and forty.
lines.title: THE ARITHMETIC DREAM
lines.subtitle: ₹60 beans + ₹30 oat milk sold for ₹240 a cup

lines.text: That is an unbelievable seventy-five percent gross margin. If you sell just one hundred and fifty cups a day, you should be pocketing three lakh rupees in monthly profit.
lines.title: THE 150 CUPS/DAY PROJECTION
lines.subtitle: Automatic cash flow before operational reality hits

name: The ₹1.5 Crore Vanity Fitout
partSub: La Marzocco machines, microcement, and the Bangalore design arms race

lines.text: Before you pour a single espresso, your bank account enters the ICU.
lines.title: DAY ZERO REALITY
lines.subtitle: Before you pour a single espresso, your capital is trapped

lines.text: Specialty coffee in Bangalore is a design arms race. You need a twelve-lakh La Marzocco machine, custom terrazzo counters, and curated Scandinavian chairs. That is one point two crores of sunk capital before opening day.
lines.title: THE DESIGN ARMS RACE
lines.subtitle: ₹12L La Marzocco + terrazzo counters + curated Scandinavian chairs

lines.text: Next comes your new best friend: the commercial landlord on 100-foot Road.
lines.title: YOUR NEW 50% PARTNER
lines.subtitle: Prime Indiranagar 100ft road commercial property deed

lines.text: He demands four lakh fifty thousand rupees a month, ten months of security deposit upfront in cash, and an automatic eight percent escalation every single year.
lines.title: 10-MONTH SECURITY DEPOSIT
lines.subtitle: ₹45 Lakhs locked in cash + guaranteed 8% annual escalation

name: The Laptop Squatter Paradox
partSub: Laptop squatters, perishable pastries, and BESCOM power bills

lines.text: In a regular restaurant, a table turns four times an afternoon. In a Bangalore specialty café, it turns zero point eight times.
lines.title: TABLE COLLAPSE
lines.subtitle: Regular restaurants turn 4x; specialty cafes turn 0.8x

lines.text: Because two senior engineers will buy one two-hundred-rupee cold brew, plug in two MacBooks, use your gigabit Wi-Fi, and conduct five Zoom sprints over six hours.
lines.title: THE SQUATTER EQUATION
lines.subtitle: Two senior techies consume 6 hours of Wi-Fi on a single ₹200 drink

name: The Physical Conveyor Belt of Spoilage

lines.text: Coffee beans last months. But artisan pastries and fresh milk do not.
lines.title: THE 24-HOUR CLOCK
lines.subtitle: Coffee beans last months; fresh pastries expire daily

lines.text: If you bake thirty sourdough sandwiches and sell twelve, the remaining eighteen go straight into the dumpster at 10:00 PM. That is an invisible thirty-thousand-rupee bleed every single month.
lines.title: THE INVISIBLE FOOD BLEED
lines.subtitle: Bake 30, sell 12... 18 artisanal sandwiches go to the dumpster at 10 PM

lines.text: Cooling a fifty-seater glass greenhouse under the April Bangalore sun requires eight split air conditioners running continuously.
lines.title: COOLING THE GREENHOUSE
lines.subtitle: 50-seater glass facade under brutal 36°C summer heat

lines.text: Between Karnataka's commercial electricity tariff and sixty liters of diesel for your backup generator, power alone eats one lakh eighty thousand rupees a month.
lines.title: NON-DOMESTIC TARIFF + DIESEL
lines.subtitle: Commercial power slab plus 60L diesel for backup generator

lines.text: A great café lives and dies by its head barista. But in Bangalore, specialty baristas are scouted like IPL cricketers.
lines.title: THE CRITICAL ASSET
lines.subtitle: Specialty baristas scouted like IPL cricketers across Bangalore

lines.text: The moment your barista masters swan latte art, the venture-funded chain across the street offers him a thirty percent raise, leaving you with burnt beans and untrained apprentices.
lines.title: THE SPECIALTY TALENT SQUEEZE
lines.subtitle: The venture-backed chain across 100ft road poaches your trained talent

name: The Whiteboard Cash-Flow Grinder
part: PART 4 · THE TRUE BALANCE SHEET & VERDICT
partSub: The mechanical cash grinder, true unit economics, and the final verdict

lines.text: When you feed your daily customer revenue through the actual operational machine, the math completely collapses.
lines.title: REVENUE MEETS REALITY
lines.subtitle: When customer cash enters the operational gear system

lines.text: Your four lakh fifty thousand rent, power, payroll, and spoilage chew up ninety percent of your incoming cash before you ever touch a single rupee.
lines.title: THE LINE-ITEM EXECUTION
lines.subtitle: Rent, BESCOM, payroll, and spoilage swallow every single note

name: The True Monthly P&L
part: PART 4 · THE TRUE BALANCE SHEET & VERDICT

lines.text: At four hundred cups a day with food, an Indiranagar café generates ten lakh rupees in gross sales.
lines.title: THE 400 CUPS/DAY CEILING
lines.subtitle: Packed weekends and full food orders on high street

lines.text: After deducting fixed rent, utilities, raw materials, GST, and payroll, the operator walks away with forty thousand rupees. In a bad monsoon month, they lose eighty-five thousand.
lines.title: THE 4% OWNER RESIDUAL
lines.subtitle: In good months: ₹40K profit. In monsoon months: -₹85K loss

name: The Secret Real Winners
part: PART 4 · THE TRUE BALANCE SHEET & VERDICT

lines.text: So who is actually making money in India's coffee boom?
lines.title: THE COFFEE BOOM PYRAMID
lines.subtitle: Follow the capital to the actual extraction point

lines.text: Not the café owner. The real winners are the commercial property owners, and the B2B specialty roasters who sell thirty-ton pallets of beans to hundreds of hopeful entrepreneurs.
lines.title: THE PICK & SHOVEL WINNERS
lines.subtitle: Selling 30-ton wholesale bean pallets to 500 hopeful entrepreneurs

name: The Final Executive Verdict
part: PART 4 · THE TRUE BALANCE SHEET & VERDICT

lines.text: If your dream is to sit in a beautiful sunlit room, drink specialty pour-overs, and curate indie playlists, do not open a café.
lines.title: SAVE YOUR CAPITAL
lines.subtitle: If you want indie pour-overs and playlists... do not open a cafe

lines.text: Just buy a six-hundred-rupee bag of beans, brew it at home, and keep your one point five crores in a simple index fund. Because opening a café in Bangalore does not make you a founder. It makes you an unpaid manager for your landlord's commercial property.
lines.title: THE COLD REALITY
lines.subtitle: You didn't become a founder. You became an unpaid manager for your landlord
